subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: Should this PR require side-effect-safe cancellation or late-write guards before merging the auth timeout backstops?
rationale: The PR fixes a serious availability failure mode, but it changes auth-provider and runtime state concurrency in ways that green tests do not settle for existing users.

options.title: Require side-effect-safe ownership
options.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime auth work cannot write credentials or active auth state after its lock, queue, or single-flight ownership has ended.

options.title: Accept the deadline-only risk
options.body: Merge the current mitigation as an availability tradeoff while explicitly owning the late credential and runtime-auth mutation risk.

options.title: Pause for auth-owner redesign
options.body: Hold this branch until an auth owner provides a cancellation or ownership-token design with live recovery proof.

recommendation.title: Require side-effect-safe ownership
recommendation.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime auth work cannot write credentials or active auth state after its lock, queue, or single-flight ownership has ended.

likelyOwner.reason: The current main blame points them at the central auth-controller and oauth-manager code paths, and the decision is about those paths’ concurrency contract.
